title.raw: 卷一百〇七 漢書9: 列傳四 史弘肇 楊邠 王章 李洪建 閻晉卿 聶文進 後贊 郭允明 劉銖 Volume 107 Book of Later Jin 9: Biographies 4 - Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, Wang Zhang, Li Hongjian, Yan Jinqing, Nie Wenjin, Hou Zan, Guo Yuming, Liu Zhu

sentences.zh: 史宏肇，字化元，鄭州滎澤人也。

translations.literal: Shi Hongzhao, styled Huayuan, was a native of Xingze in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao, whose style was Huayuan, came from Xingze in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 父潘，本田家。

translations.literal: His father Pan was originally a field household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pan had originally been registered as a farming household.

sentences.zh: 宏肇少遊俠無行，拳勇健步，日行二百里，走及奔馬。

translations.literal: Hongzhao in youth roamed as a knight-errant without proper conduct; he was brave in boxing and swift of foot, traveling two hundred li in a day and running abreast of galloping horses.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Hongzhao lived as an unruly bravo, famed for his fists and his legs: he could cover two hundred li in a day and keep pace with a running horse.

sentences.zh: 梁末，每七戶出一兵，宏肇在籍中，後隸本州開道都，選入禁軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang, one soldier was levied from every seven households; Hongzhao was on the rolls, later attached to the prefecture's Kaodao command, and selected into the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Liang was failing, every seven households had to supply one soldier; Hongzhao was conscripted, later assigned to the prefectural Kaodao command, and then chosen for the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 嘗在晉祖麾下，遂留為親從，及踐阼，用為控鶴小校。

translations.literal: He once served under the Jin founder and was kept as a personal follower; when the founder took the throne, he was made a junior officer of the Cranes Controlling Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He had served under the Jin founder and stayed on as a personal attendant; when that ruler acceded, Hongzhao was appointed a junior officer in the Cranes Controlling Guard.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮太原，奏請從行，升為牙校，後置武節左右指揮，以宏肇為都將，遙領雷州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu held Taiyuan, he memorialized asking Hongzhao to accompany him on campaign; he was promoted to aide-de-camp, and later when the Left and Right Commands of Martial Valor were established, Hongzhao was made their commander-in-chief and held the post of Leizhou prefect in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu governed Taiyuan he asked that Hongzhao march with him and raised him to aide-de-camp; later, when the Left and Right Commands of Martial Valor were formed, Hongzhao became their commander-in-chief and was given Leizhou in absentia.

sentences.zh: 高祖建號之初，代州王暉叛，以城歸契丹，宏肇征之，一鼓而拔，尋授許州節度使，充侍衛步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's founding of the state, Wang Hui of Daizhou rebelled and surrendered the city to the Khitan; Hongzhao campaigned against him and took it at the first assault, and soon after was made military governor of Xuzhou and commander of the Palace Guard infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Gaozu founded the dynasty, Wang Hui of Daizhou rebelled and handed his city to the Khitan; Hongzhao attacked, took it at the first blow, and was soon made military governor of Xuzhou and commander of the palace guard infantry.

sentences.zh: 會王守恩以上黨求附，契丹主命大將耿崇美率眾登太行，欲取上黨，高祖命宏肇以軍應援。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Shou'en sought to attach himself with Shangdang; the Khitan ruler ordered the great general Geng Chongmei to lead troops over the Taihang range to seize Shangdang, and Gaozu ordered Hongzhao to go with an army in support.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shou'en offered Shangdang in submission, the Khitan ruler sent the general Geng Chongmei over the Taihang to take it, and Gaozu ordered Hongzhao to march in relief.

sentences.zh: 軍至潞州，契丹退去，翟令奇以澤州迎降。

translations.literal: When the army reached Luzhou the Khitan withdrew, and Zhai Lingqi welcomed them by surrendering Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Luzhou the Khitan pulled back, and Zhai Lingqi surrendered Zezhou to the Han forces.

sentences.zh: 會河陽武行德遣人迎宏肇，遂率眾南下，與行德合。

translations.literal: It happened that Wu Xingde of Heyang sent men to welcome Hongzhao, whereupon he led his troops south and joined Xingde.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingde of Heyang then sent envoys to welcome Hongzhao, who marched south and joined forces with him.

sentences.zh: 故高祖由蒲、陜赴洛如歸，宏肇前鋒之功也。

translations.literal: Thus when Gaozu went from Pu and Shaan to Luoyang it was as though he were returning home—this was due to Hongzhao's merit as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: That Gaozu could travel from Pu and Shaan to Luoyang as if he were merely going home was largely Hongzhao's work as the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 宏肇嚴毅寡言，部轄軍眾，有過無舍，兵士所至，秋毫不犯。

translations.literal: Hongzhao was stern, resolute, and sparing of speech; in commanding troops he showed no mercy for offenses, and wherever his soldiers went not even a hair was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao was severe, taciturn, and relentless with discipline: his men took nothing from the people they passed.

sentences.zh: 部下有指揮使，嘗因指使少不從命，宏肇立撾殺之，將吏股栗，以至平定兩京，無敢幹忤。

translations.literal: Among his subordinates was a commander who once, because his orders were slightly disobeyed, was immediately clubbed to death by Hongzhao; officers and clerks trembled in their legs, so that down to the pacification of the two capitals none dared oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Once a subordinate commander balked at a minor order and Hongzhao had him beaten to death on the spot; from that day his officers shook with fear, and through the pacification of the two capitals no one dared cross him.

sentences.zh: 從駕征鄴回，加同平章事，充侍衛親軍都指揮使，兼鎮宋州。

translations.literal: On returning from accompanying the emperor on the campaign against Ye, he was advanced to co-equal Grand Counsellor, made commander of the Palace Guard, and concurrently given charge of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Ye campaign he was made co-equal Grand Counsellor, commander of the palace guard, and concurrent governor of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖大漸，與樞密使楊邠、周太祖、蘇逢吉等同受顧命。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was gravely ill, together with Military Affairs Commissioner Yang Bin, Zhou Taizu, Su Fengji, and others he received the dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: As Gaozu lay dying, Hongzhao received the final charge along with Yang Bin, Zhou Taizu, Su Fengji, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 隱帝嗣位，加檢校太師、兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yin succeeded, Hongzhao was further made Honorary Grand Preceptor and concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yin came to the throne, Hongzhao was given the honorary rank of Grand Preceptor and made Palace Attendant as well.

sentences.zh: 居無何，河中、永興、鳳翔連橫謀叛，關輔大擾，朝廷日有征發，群情憂揣，亦有不逞之徒，妄構虛語，流布京師。

translations.literal: Before long, Hezhong, Yongxing, and Fengxiang joined in plotting rebellion, the Guanzhong region was greatly disturbed, the court had levies day after day, public feeling was anxious and fearful, and there were also unruly men who falsely fabricated rumors and spread them through the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hezhong, Yongxing, and Fengxiang were in league to rebel; the Guanzhong heartland was in turmoil, levies followed one after another, and fear spread through the city along with wild rumors invented by malcontents.

sentences.zh: 宏肇都轄禁軍，警衛都邑，專行刑殺，略無顧避，無賴之輩，望風匿跡，路有遺棄，人不敢取。

translations.literal: Hongzhao commanded the palace guard, guarded the capital, and carried out executions exclusively, with scarcely any hesitation; ruffians hid at the sight of him, and though goods lay abandoned on the road, no one dared take them.
translations.idiomatic: As head of the palace guard he policed the capital and killed without scruple; thugs vanished at his approach, and even goods left in the street went untouched.

sentences.zh: 然而不問罪之輕重，理之所在，但雲有犯，便處極刑，枉濫之家，莫敢上訴。

translations.literal: Yet he did not inquire into the lightness or heaviness of offenses or where right lay; if one merely said there was a violation, the extreme penalty was imposed, and households wronged had none who dared appeal.
translations.idiomatic: He paid no heed to whether a charge was grave or petty or even true: any report of wrongdoing brought death, and families unjustly condemned dared not appeal.

sentences.zh: 巡司軍吏，因緣為奸，嫁禍脅人，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Patrol officers and military clerks took advantage of this to practice villainy, shifting blame and coercing people, in cases too numerous to record.
translations.idiomatic: Patrolmen and army clerks used the climate to frame rivals and extort the innocent beyond counting.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·邊歸讜傳》：史宏肇怙權專殺，閭裏告訐成風，歸讜言曰：「邇來有匿名書及言風聞事，構害良善，有傷風化，遂使貪吏得以報復私怨，讒夫得以肆其虛誕。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Bian Guiyan in the Song History: Shi Hongzhao relied on power and killed at will; denunciation in the neighborhoods became the fashion. Guiyan said: "Recently there have been anonymous letters and reports of hearsay matters that frame and harm the good, injuring public morals, so that greedy officials can avenge private grudges and slanderers can indulge their fabrications.
translations.idiomatic: (The Song History biography of Bian Guiyan records that under Shi Hongzhao's arbitrary killings, informers flourished in every lane. Guiyan urged the throne: "Anonymous letters and rumor-mongering lately frame honest men and poison public life, letting greedy officials settle private scores and letting slanderers run wild.

sentences.zh: 請明行條制，禁遏誣妄，凡顯有披論，具陳姓名。

translations.literal: I ask that regulations be clearly promulgated to forbid and stop false accusations; whenever there is an open accusation, the accuser's name should be fully stated.
translations.idiomatic: Issue clear rules against false denunciation: every open charge must name its author.

sentences.zh: 其匿名書及風聞事者，並見止絕。

translations.literal: As for anonymous letters and hearsay matters, let them all be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Anonymous letters and hearsay accusations should be stopped altogether."

sentences.zh: 」論者韙之。）〉

translations.literal: " Commentators approved. Closing editorial bracket.)
translations.idiomatic: Commentators approved his proposal.) Editorial bracket closing the comment block.

sentences.zh: 時太白晝見，民有仰觀者，為坊正所拘，立斷其腰領。

translations.literal: At the time Venus appeared in daylight; a commoner who looked up at it was seized by the ward head and immediately beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: When Venus was seen by day, a man who looked up at the sky was seized by his ward officer and beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 又有醉民抵忤一軍士，則誣以訛言棄市。

translations.literal: Again, a drunken commoner who offended a soldier was falsely charged with spreading sedition and executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: A drunk who jostled a soldier was accused of spreading sedition and put to death in the market.

sentences.zh: 其他斷舌、決口、斫筋、折足者，僅無虛日。

translations.literal: As for others whose tongues were cut, mouths split, sinews severed, or feet broken, scarcely a day passed without such cases.
translations.idiomatic: Tongues cut out, mouths split, tendons severed, feet broken—hardly a day passed without such punishments.

sentences.zh: 故相李崧為部曲誣告，族戮於市，取其幼女為婢。

translations.literal: The former chief minister Li Song was falsely denounced by his retainers; his clan was executed in the market, and his young daughter was taken as a maidservant.
translations.idiomatic: The former chief minister Li Song was framed by his own retainers; his whole clan was slaughtered in the market, and his young daughter was made a servant girl.

sentences.zh: 自是仕宦之家畜仆隸者，皆以姑息為意，而舊勛故將失勢之後，為廝養輩之所脅制者，往往有之。

translations.literal: From this time households of officials who kept servants and slaves all treated them with indulgence, while former meritorious generals after losing power were often coerced by menials.
translations.idiomatic: After that, official households indulged their servants for fear of denunciation, and many once-great generals, fallen from power, found themselves bullied by the very men who waited on them.

sentences.zh: 軍司孔目吏解暉，性狡而酷，凡有推劾，隨意鍛煉。

translations.literal: The army bureau clerk Xie Hui was by nature cunning and cruel; in every investigation he forged evidence as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The army clerk Xie Hui was sly and pitiless; in every case he tortured confessions as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 人有抵軍禁者，被其苦楚，無不自誣以求死所，都人遇之，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: Anyone who ran afoul of military law, once subjected to his torments, all confessed falsely to seek a place of death; when people of the capital met him, none dared look up.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone caught in his grip confessed to anything to escape further torture; in the capital people lowered their eyes when he passed.

sentences.zh: 有燕人何福殷者，以商販為業。

translations.literal: There was a man of Yan named He Fuyin who made his living as a merchant.
translations.idiomatic: A merchant of Yan named He Fuyin traded for his living.

sentences.zh: 嘗以十四萬市得玉枕，遣家僮及商人李進賣於淮南，易茗而回。

translations.literal: He once bought a jade pillow for one hundred forty thousand cash, sent his house servant and the merchant Li Jin to sell it in Huainan, and returned after exchanging it for tea.
translations.idiomatic: He once paid one hundred forty thousand cash for a jade pillow and sent his servant and a trader named Li Jin to sell it in Huainan for tea.

sentences.zh: 家僮無行，隱福殷貨財數十萬，福殷責其償，不伏，遂杖之。

translations.literal: The house servant was without proper conduct and concealed several hundred thousand of Fuyin's goods; Fuyin demanded repayment, he would not submit, and Fuyin had him beaten.
translations.idiomatic: The servant was worthless and embezzled hundreds of thousands from him; when Fuyin demanded repayment the man refused and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 未幾，家僮詣宏肇上變，言契丹主之入汴也，趙延壽遣福殷賫玉枕陰遺淮南，以致誠意。

translations.literal: Before long the house servant went to Hongzhao to report a matter of urgency, saying that when the Khitan ruler entered Bian, Zhao Yanshou had sent Fuyin bearing the jade pillow to present it secretly to Huainan as a token of goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the servant denounced his master to Hongzhao, claiming that when the Khitan took Bian, Zhao Yanshou had sent Fuyin with the jade pillow as a secret gift to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 宏肇即日遣捕福殷等系之。

translations.literal: Hongzhao that same day sent men to arrest Fuyin and the others and bind them.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao had Fuyin and the others arrested that very day.

sentences.zh: 解暉希旨，榜掠備至，福殷自誣，連罪者數輩，並棄市。

translations.literal: Xie Hui to please his intent applied flogging to the full; Fuyin confessed falsely, and several others implicated with him were all executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui tortured them to please his master; Fuyin confessed under the lash, several others were implicated, and all were executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 妻女為宏肇帳下分取之，其家財籍沒。

translations.literal: His wife and daughters were divided among Hongzhao's personal staff, and his household property was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and daughters were divided among Hongzhao's retainers, and his estate was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 宏肇不喜賓客，嘗言：「文人難耐，輕我輩，謂我輩為卒，可恨可恨！

translations.literal: Hongzhao did not like guests and once said: "Literati are hard to bear—they look down on men like us and call us soldiers. Hateful, hateful!
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao disliked entertaining guests and once said, "Scholars are unbearable—they despise men like us and call us common soldiers. Detestable, detestable!

sentences.zh: 」宏肇所領睢陽，其屬府公利，委親吏楊乙就府檢校，貪戾兇橫，負勢生事，吏民畏之，副戎已下，望風展敬。

translations.literal: " Suiyang, which Hongzhao held, had its prefectural revenues; he entrusted his intimate clerk Yang Yi to inspect the prefecture, and Yi was greedy, cruel, and overbearing, using power to stir up trouble; officials and people feared him, and from deputy commanders down all showed deference at his approach.
translations.idiomatic: " In Suiyang, which Hongzhao governed, he put his crony Yang Yi in charge of the prefectural accounts. Yi was greedy, brutal, and fond of trouble; officials and commoners alike feared him, and even deputy commanders bowed when he appeared.

sentences.zh: 聚劍刻剝，無所不至，月率萬緡，以輸宏肇，一境之內，嫉之如仇。

translations.literal: He extorted by every means, delivering ten thousand strings of cash a month to Hongzhao; within the whole circuit they hated him as an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He squeezed the region by every trick and sent Hongzhao ten thousand strings of cash a month; the whole circuit hated him as they would a foe.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·薛居正傳》：史宏肇領侍衛親軍，威震人主，殘忍自恣，人莫敢忤其意。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Xue Juzheng in the Outline History of the Eastern Capital: Shi Hongzhao commanded the palace guard; his might awed the ruler, he was cruel and willful, and none dared go against his intent.
translations.idiomatic: (The Outline History of the Eastern Capital biography of Xue Juzheng notes that Shi Hongzhao, commanding the palace guard, awed even the emperor, ruled by cruelty, and brooked no opposition.

sentences.zh: 其部下吏告民犯鹽禁，法當死。

translations.literal: A subordinate clerk reported that a commoner had violated the salt prohibition, for which the law required death.
translations.idiomatic: One of his clerks reported a salt smuggler who by law deserved death.

sentences.zh: 居正疑其不實，召詰之，乃其吏以私憾而誣之也。

translations.literal: Juzheng doubted that it was true, summoned and questioned him, and it turned out the clerk had falsely accused him out of private resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng doubted the charge, questioned the man, and found the clerk had framed him out of spite.

sentences.zh: 逮捕吏鞫之，具伏，以吏抵法。

translations.literal: He arrested the clerk and interrogated him; the clerk fully confessed, and the clerk was punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He arrested the clerk, obtained a full confession, and punished the accuser instead.

sentences.zh: 宏肇雖怒甚，竟亦無以屈也。）〉

translations.literal: Hongzhao was very angry, but in the end had no way to bend him. Closing editorial bracket.)
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao was furious but could not make Juzheng yield.) Editorial bracket closing the comment block.

sentences.zh: 周太祖平河中班師，推功於眾，以宏肇有翊衛鎮重之功，言之於隱帝，即授兼中書令。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu pacified Hezhong and returned the army, attributing merit to the host, he spoke to Emperor Yin of Hongzhao's merit in supporting and guarding the throne, and Hongzhao was at once made concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Taizu pacified Hezhong he credited the army but told Emperor Yin that Hongzhao deserved praise for guarding the throne; Hongzhao was then made concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 隱帝自關西賊平之後，昵近小人，太后親族，頗行幹托，宏肇與楊邠甚不平之。

translations.literal: After the rebels in the Guanxi region were pacified, Emperor Yin grew close to petty men and the empress dowager's kin, who frequently pressed requests; Hongzhao and Yang Bin were very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: After the western rebels were crushed, Emperor Yin favored petty courtiers and the empress dowager's relatives, who pressed their requests freely; Hongzhao and Yang Bin were deeply offended.

sentences.zh: 太后有故人子求補軍職，宏肇怒而斬之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager had an old acquaintance's son who sought appointment in the army; Hongzhao in anger beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager's protégé sought a post in the army, Hongzhao had him beheaded in a rage.

sentences.zh: 帝始聽樂，賜教坊使玉帶，諸伶官錦袍，往謝宏肇，宏肇讓之曰：「健兒為國戍邊，忍寒冒暑，未能遍有沾賜，爾輩何功，敢當此賜！

translations.literal: The emperor first began listening to music and bestowed jade belts on the directors of the Music Bureau and brocade robes on the players; they went to thank Hongzhao, who rebuked them, saying: "Stalwart soldiers guard the borders for the state, enduring cold and heat, yet cannot all receive such favors—what merit have you to dare accept this reward!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first took up music he gave jade belts to the directors of the Music Bureau and brocade robes to the players; they came to thank Hongzhao, who scolded them: "Soldiers on the frontier endure cold and heat and still go unrewarded—what have you done to deserve this?

sentences.zh: 」盡取袍帶還官，其兇戾如此。

translations.literal: " He took all the robes and belts back to the office; he was so fierce and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: " He seized the gifts and returned them to the treasury—so brutal was his temper.

sentences.zh: 周太祖有鎮鄴之命，宏肇欲兼領機樞之任，蘇逢吉異其議，宏肇忿之。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu received the command to govern Ye, Hongzhao wished also to hold the post at the military secretariat; Su Fengji differed from his view, and Hongzhao resented him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu was sent to govern Ye, Hongzhao wanted to keep the military secretariat as well; Su Fengji disagreed, and Hongzhao bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 翌日，因竇貞固飲會，貴臣悉集，宏肇厲色舉爵屬周太祖曰：「昨晨廷論，一何同異！

translations.literal: The next day, at a drinking gathering hosted by Dou Zhengu, all the great ministers assembled; Hongzhao with stern countenance raised his cup and addressed Zhou Taizu: "Yesterday morning's court debate—how great the disagreement!
translations.idiomatic: The next day at a banquet given by Dou Zhengu, Hongzhao glared and raised his cup to Zhou Taizu: "Yesterday's debate in court—what a quarrel that was!

sentences.zh: 今日與弟飲此。

translations.literal: Today let younger brother drink this.
translations.idiomatic: Today younger brother, drink with me."

sentences.zh: 」楊邠、蘇逢吉亦舉大爵曰：「此國家之事也，何足介意！

translations.literal: " Yang Bin and Su Fengji also raised great cups and said: "This is a matter of state—what is there to take to heart!
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Bin and Su Fengji raised their cups as well: "These are affairs of state—why take offense?

sentences.zh: 」俱飲釂。

translations.literal: " All drank to the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: " All drained their cups.

sentences.zh: 宏肇又厲聲言曰：「安朝廷，定禍亂，直須長槍大劍，至如毛錐子，焉足用哉！

translations.literal: Hongzhao again spoke in a harsh voice: "To secure the court and settle turmoil one needs only long spears and great swords—as for hair-brush pens, of what use are they!
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao shouted again, "To steady the court and end chaos you need long spears and great swords—what use are writing brushes!

sentences.zh: 」三司使王章曰：「雖有長槍大劍，若無毛錐子，贍軍財賦，自何而集？

translations.literal: " Director of the Three Agencies Wang Zhang said: "Though there are long spears and great swords, without hair-brush pens, from where would funds to supply the army be gathered?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Zhang, director of the Three Agencies, replied, "Even with spears and swords, without brushes where would the money to feed the army come from?

sentences.zh: 」宏肇默然，少頃而罷。

translations.literal: " Hongzhao was silent, and after a little while the gathering broke up.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongzhao fell silent, and soon the party ended.

sentences.zh: 未幾，三司使王章於其第張酒樂，時宏肇與宰相、樞密使及內客省使閻晉卿等俱會。

translations.literal: Before long, Director Wang Zhang spread wine and music at his residence; at the time Hongzhao met together with the chief ministers, the military affairs commissioners, and Commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau Yan Jinqing and others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Zhang gave a feast at his house; Hongzhao came with the chief ministers, the military commissioners, and Yan Jinqing of the Inner Guests Bureau.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，為手勢令，宏肇不熟其事，而閻晉卿坐次宏肇，屢教之。

translations.literal: When the wine was deep they played the hand-gesture drinking game; Hongzhao was not skilled in it, and Yan Jinqing, seated next to Hongzhao, repeatedly instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: As the drinking deepened they played hand-signal forfeits; Hongzhao did not know the game, and Yan Jinqing beside him kept coaching him.

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉戲宏肇曰：「近坐有姓閻人，何憂罰爵！

translations.literal: Su Fengji jested with Hongzhao: "There is a man surnamed Yan seated nearby—why worry about penalty cups!
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji teased him: "You have a Yan sitting right beside you—why fear a forfeit cup?

sentences.zh: 」宏肇妻閻氏，本酒妓也，宏肇謂逢吉譏之，大怒，以醜語詬逢吉。

translations.literal: " Hongzhao's wife was the Yan clan; she had originally been a wine-house entertainer. Hongzhao thought Fengji was mocking him and in great anger cursed Fengji with foul language.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongzhao's wife was surnamed Yan and had once been a tavern singer; he took Fengji's joke as a slur on her and cursed him foully.

sentences.zh: 逢吉不校，宏肇欲毆逢吉，逢吉策馬而去，宏肇遽起索劍，意欲追逢吉。

translations.literal: Fengji did not contend; Hongzhao wished to beat Fengji, who spurred his horse and fled; Hongzhao sprang up to seek a sword, intending to pursue Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji would not answer back; Hongzhao tried to strike him, but Fengji rode off, and Hongzhao leapt up for a sword to give chase.

sentences.zh: 楊邠曰：「蘇公是宰相，公若害之，致天子何地，公細思之！

translations.literal: Yang Bin said: "Master Su is chief minister—if you harm him, where will that leave the Son of Heaven? Think carefully!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin cried, "Su is chief minister—if you kill him, what becomes of the emperor? Think again!

sentences.zh: 」邠泣下。

translations.literal: " Bin wept.
translations.idiomatic: " He wept as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 宏肇索馬急馳而去，邠慮有非常，連鑣而進，送至第而還。

translations.literal: Hongzhao sought a horse and galloped away in haste; Bin feared something extraordinary and rode close behind, escorting him to his residence before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao galloped home; fearing worse, Bin rode after him and did not turn back until he had seen him inside his gate.

sentences.zh: 自是將相不協如水火矣。

translations.literal: From this time the generals and ministers were as incompatible as fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the generals and ministers were at odds like fire and water.

sentences.zh: 隱帝遣王峻將酒樂於公子亭以和之，竟不能解。

translations.literal: Emperor Yin sent Wang Jun with wine and music to the Prince's Son Pavilion to reconcile them, but in the end could not resolve it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yin sent Wang Jun with wine and music to the Prince's Son Pavilion to patch things up, but the breach could not be healed.

sentences.zh: 其後李業、郭允明、後贊、聶文進居中用事，不悅執政。

translations.literal: Afterward Li Ye, Guo Yunming, Hou Zan, and Nie Wenjin held power within the palace and were displeased with those in charge of government.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Ye, Guo Yunming, Hou Zan, and Nie Wenjin held sway in the palace and resented the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 又見隱帝年漸長，厭為大臣所制，嘗有忿言，業等乃乘間譖宏肇等，隱帝稍以為信。

translations.literal: They also saw that Emperor Yin was gradually growing older and resented being controlled by great ministers; he sometimes spoke in anger, and Ye and the others seized the opportunity to slander Hongzhao and the rest; the emperor gradually came to believe them.
translations.idiomatic: They saw too that Emperor Yin was maturing and chafed under ministerial control; when he spoke bitterly, Ye and his circle slandered Hongzhao and the others until the emperor began to believe them.

sentences.zh: 業等乃言宏肇等專權震主，終必為亂，隱帝益恐。

translations.literal: Ye and the others then said that Hongzhao and the rest monopolized power and awed the ruler, and would surely end in rebellion; Emperor Yin grew still more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: They told him Hongzhao's faction monopolized power, awed the throne, and would surely rebel; the emperor grew more afraid.

sentences.zh: 嘗一夕，聞作坊鍛甲之聲，疑外有兵仗卒至，達旦不寐。

translations.literal: Once one night he heard the sound of armor being forged in the workshops and suspected that armed troops outside had suddenly arrived; he did not sleep until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: One night he heard armor being hammered in the workshops, imagined troops had come upon him, and lay awake until dawn.

sentences.zh: 自是與業等密謀禁中，欲誅宏肇等。

translations.literal: From this time he secretly plotted within the palace with Ye and the others to execute Hongzhao and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He then plotted secretly in the palace with Ye and the others to kill Hongzhao and his allies.

sentences.zh: 議定，入白太后，太后曰：「此事豈可輕發耶！

translations.literal: When the plan was settled he went in to inform the empress dowager; the empress dowager said: "How can this matter be lightly launched!
translations.idiomatic: When the plan was set he told the empress dowager, who said, "Such a thing must not be undertaken lightly!

sentences.zh: 更問宰臣等。

translations.literal: Ask the chief ministers again.
translations.idiomatic: Consult the chief ministers again."

sentences.zh: 」李業在側，曰：「先皇帝言，朝廷大事，莫共措大商量。

translations.literal: " Li Ye was at her side and said: "The late emperor said that on great affairs of court one must not consult with the 'coarse fellows.'
translations.idiomatic: " Li Ye at her side said, "The late emperor warned never to discuss great affairs of state with those coarse fellows."

sentences.zh: 」太后又言之，隱帝怒曰：「閨門之內，焉知國家之事！

translations.literal: " The empress dowager spoke again; Emperor Yin angrily said: "Within the women's quarters, how would one know affairs of state!
translations.idiomatic: " When she repeated her warning, Emperor Yin flared up: "What do women behind the curtain know of statecraft!

sentences.zh: 」拂衣而出。

translations.literal: " He brushed his robes and went out.
translations.idiomatic: " He stormed out.

sentences.zh: 內客省使閻晉卿潛知其事，乃詣宏肇私第，將欲告之，宏肇以他事拒之不見。

translations.literal: Commissioner Yan Jinqing of the Inner Guests Bureau secretly knew of the matter and went to Hongzhao's private residence intending to inform him, but Hongzhao refused to see him on the pretext of other business.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jinqing of the Inner Guests Bureau learned of the plot and went to warn Hongzhao at his home, but Hongzhao refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 乾祐三年冬十一月十三日，宏肇入朝，與樞密使楊邠、三司使王章同坐於廣政殿東廡下，俄有甲士數十人自內而出，害宏肇等於閣，夷其族。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the eleventh month of winter in the third year of Qianyou, Hongzhao entered court; together with Military Affairs Commissioner Yang Bin and Director Wang Zhang he sat beneath the eastern veranda of the Hall of Broad Governance, when suddenly several tens of armored soldiers came out from within and killed Hongzhao and the others at the pavilion, exterminating their clans.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the eleventh month of Qianyou 3, Hongzhao attended court and sat with Yang Bin and Wang Zhang under the eastern veranda of the Hall of Broad Governance; suddenly dozens of armored men emerged from within, killed Hongzhao and his allies in the pavilion, and exterminated their families.

sentences.zh: 先是，宏肇第數有異，嘗一日，於階砌隙中有煙氣蓬勃而出。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hongzhao's residence had repeatedly shown strange signs; once on a day smoke billowed forth from a crack in the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Before his fall his house had shown omens more than once; one day smoke poured from a crack in the courtyard steps.

sentences.zh: 禍前二日昧爽，有星落於宏肇前三數步，如迸火而散，俄而被誅。

translations.literal: Two days before the calamity, at dawn, a star fell three or four paces before Hongzhao and scattered like bursting fire; soon after he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before his death, at dawn, a meteor fell a few paces before him and burst like flame; soon he was killed.

sentences.zh: 周太祖踐阼，追封鄭王，以禮葬，官為立碑。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Hongzhao as Prince of Zheng, buried him with proper rites, and had officials erect a stele.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Taizu came to the throne he posthumously made Hongzhao Prince of Zheng, buried him with full honors, and had a stele set up.

sentences.zh: 宏肇子德充，乾祐中，授檢校司空，領忠州刺史。

translations.literal: Hongzhao's son Dechong, during Qianyou, was made Honorary Minister of Works and given charge of Zhongzhou as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao's son Dechong, in the Qianyou era, was made Honorary Minister of Works and prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 粗讀書，親儒者，常不悅父之所為。

translations.literal: He had read books in a rough way, was close to Confucian scholars, and often disapproved of his father's conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He had some learning, favored scholars, and often disapproved of his father's ways.

sentences.zh: 貢院嘗錄一學科於省門叫噪，申中書門下，宰相蘇逢吉令送侍衛司，請痛笞刺面。

translations.literal: Once the examination yard enrolled a candidate in one subject who made an uproar at the provincial gate; the matter was reported to the Secretariat and Chancellery, and chief minister Su Fengji ordered him sent to the Palace Guard bureau with a request for severe flogging and facial tattooing.
translations.idiomatic: Once an examinee who had passed one subject made a disturbance at the provincial gate; Su Fengji ordered him handed to the palace guard for a severe beating and facial tattoo.

sentences.zh: 德充聞之，白父曰：「書生無禮，有府縣御史臺，非軍務治也。

translations.literal: When Dechong heard of it he told his father: "The scholar was without propriety, but there are prefectural, county, and censorial offices—this is not a matter for military jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Dechong told his father, "The man was rude, but prefects, magistrates, and the censorate exist for that—this is not a soldier's affair.

sentences.zh: 公卿如此，蓋欲彰大人之過。

translations.literal: For the chief ministers to act thus is surely to display the great man's fault.
translations.idiomatic: If ministers treat him so harshly, they only want to expose your excesses."

sentences.zh: 」宏肇深以為然，即破械放之。

translations.literal: " Hongzhao deeply agreed, immediately broke his fetters, and released him.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongzhao saw the point, broke his bonds, and set him free.

sentences.zh: 後之識者尤嘉德充之為人焉。

translations.literal: Later men of discernment especially praised Dechong's character.
translations.idiomatic: Later observers especially admired Dechong's character.

sentences.zh: 楊邠，魏州冠氏人也。

translations.literal: Yang Bin was a native of Guanshi in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin came from Guanshi in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 少以吏給事使府，後唐租庸使孔謙，即其妻之世父也。

translations.literal: In youth he served as a clerk in the commissionerer's office; Kong Qian, grain-and-corvée commissioner of Later Tang, was his wife's father's cousin.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he clerked in a military commissioner's office; Kong Qian, Later Tang's grain-and-corvée commissioner, was his wife's uncle.

sentences.zh: 謙領度支，補勾押官，歷孟、華、鄆三州糧料使。

translations.literal: When Qian headed revenue, Bin was appointed checking-and-custody clerk and served successively as grain commissioner of Meng, Hua, and Yan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian ran the revenue bureau, Bin became a checking clerk and served as grain commissioner in Meng, Hua, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 高祖為鄴都留守，用為左都押衙，高祖鎮太原，益加親委。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was military governor of the Ye capital, he employed Bin as left chief aide-de-camp; when Gaozu held Taiyuan, he entrusted him still more closely.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was governor of the Ye capital he made Bin his left chief aide; when Gaozu moved to Taiyuan he relied on him still more.

sentences.zh: 漢國建，遷檢校太保、權樞密使。

translations.literal: When the Han state was founded, he was transferred to Honorary Grand Guardian and acting Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty was founded he was made Honorary Grand Guardian and acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 汴、洛平，正拜樞密使、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When Bian and Luo were pacified, he was formally appointed Military Affairs Commissioner and Honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: After Bian and Luoyang were secured he was formally made military commissioner and Honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 及高祖大漸，與蘇逢吉、史宏肇等同受顧命，輔立嗣君。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was gravely ill, together with Su Fengji, Shi Hongzhao, and others he received the dying charge to assist in establishing the heir.
translations.idiomatic: As Gaozu lay dying he received the final charge along with Su Fengji and Shi Hongzhao to help install the heir.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，宰臣李濤上章，請出邠與周太祖為藩鎮，邠等泣訴於太后，由是罷濤而相邠，加中書侍郎兼吏部尚書、同平章事，仍兼樞密使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yin took the throne, chief minister Li Tao memorialized asking that Bin and Zhou Taizu be sent out as frontier governors; Bin and the others wept and appealed to the empress dowager, whereupon Tao was dismissed and Bin made chief minister, advanced to Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent Minister of Personnel and co-equal Grand Counsellor, still holding the military commissionership.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yin succeeded, Li Tao urged that Yang Bin and Zhou Taizu be sent to the provinces; Bin wept before the empress dowager, Tao was removed, and Bin became chief minister with the posts of Vice Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Personnel, co-equal Grand Counsellor, and military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時中書除吏太多，訛謬者眾。

translations.literal: At the time the Secretariat appointed too many officials, and errors were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat had been appointing too many officials, and mistakes were common.

sentences.zh: 及邠居相位，帝一以委之，凡南衙奏事，中書除命，先委邠斟酌，如不出邠意，至於一簿一掾，亦不聽從。

translations.literal: When Bin held the chief minister's post, the emperor entrusted everything to him; all matters reported from the southern offices and all Secretariat appointments were first referred to Bin for deliberation, and if they did not accord with Bin's intent, even down to a single clerk or aide, they were not approved.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bin was chief minister the emperor left everything to him: every report from the outer offices and every appointment passed through Bin first, and nothing—not even a minor clerk—went through if he disapproved.

sentences.zh: 邠雖長於吏事，不識大體，常言：「為國家者，但得帑藏豐盈，甲兵強盛，至於文章禮樂，並是虛事，何足介意也。

translations.literal: Though Bin was skilled in clerical affairs, he did not grasp the larger pattern and often said: "For the state, one need only have the treasury full and armor and weapons strong—as for literature and ritual music, they are all empty matters, what is there to mind?
translations.idiomatic: Bin was adept at paperwork but blind to larger matters, and often said, "A state needs only a full treasury and strong armies; literature and ritual are empty trifles not worth a thought.

sentences.zh: 」平河中，邠加右僕射。

translations.literal: " When Hezhong was pacified, Bin was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: " After Hezhong was pacified he was made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 邠既專國政，觸事苛細，條理煩碎。

translations.literal: Once Bin monopolized state affairs, he was harsh and minute in every matter, with regulations tedious and fragmented.
translations.idiomatic: With sole control of government he was petty in everything and buried the realm in minute rules.

sentences.zh: 前資官不得於外方居止，自京師至諸州府，行人往來，並須給公憑。

translations.literal: Former officials were not permitted to reside outside the capital; from the capital to every prefecture and district, travelers coming and going all had to be issued official passes.
translations.idiomatic: Retired officials could not live outside the capital, and every traveler between the capital and the provinces needed an official pass.

sentences.zh: 所由司求請公憑者，朝夕填咽，旬日之間，民情大擾，行路擁塞，邠乃止其事。

translations.literal: Those who sought passes from the responsible offices filled the gates morning and evening; within ten days public feeling was greatly disturbed and the roads clogged, and Bin then stopped the measure.
translations.idiomatic: Offices issuing passes were jammed day and night; within ten days the people were in an uproar and the roads blocked, and Bin abandoned the scheme.

sentences.zh: 時史宏肇恣行慘酷，殺戮日眾，都人士庶，相目於路，邠但稱宏肇之善。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Hongzhao practiced cruelty at will and killings grew daily; gentlemen and commoners of the capital exchanged glances in the streets, yet Bin only praised Hongzhao's merits.
translations.idiomatic: While Shi Hongzhao slaughtered ever more freely and people in the capital exchanged fearful glances in the street, Bin spoke only of Hongzhao's virtues.

sentences.zh: 太后弟武德使李業求為宣徽使，隱帝與太后重違之，私訪於邠，邠以朝廷內使，遷拜有序，不可超居，遂止。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's younger brother Li Ye, commissioner of Wude, sought to become commissioner of the Palace Attendants; Emperor Yin and the empress dowager were deeply unwilling but privately consulted Bin, who said that inner palace commissioners had an orderly sequence of promotion and could not be skipped over, and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's brother Li Ye wanted the post of palace attendant commissioner; though emperor and dowager disliked it, Bin told them privately that inner posts had a fixed order of promotion and could not be jumped, and the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 隱帝所愛耿夫人，欲立為後，邠亦以為太速。

translations.literal: Lady Geng, whom Emperor Yin favored, was to be made empress; Bin also thought it too soon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make his favorite Lady Geng empress; Bin thought the move premature.

sentences.zh: 夫人卒，隱帝欲以後禮葬，邠又止之，隱帝意不悅，左右有承間進甘言者，隱帝益怒之。

translations.literal: When the lady died, Emperor Yin wished to bury her with empress rites; Bin again stopped it; the emperor was displeased, and attendants who seized the opportunity offered sweet words, so the emperor grew still angrier at Bin.
translations.idiomatic: When she died the emperor wanted empress funeral rites; Bin refused again. Courtiers who seized the moment flattered the emperor, and his anger at Bin deepened.
