translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （案：此下疑有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: below this point the text is suspected of being defective.) Closing editorial bracket.)
translations.idiomatic: (Editor's note: text appears missing below.) Editorial bracket closing the comment block.

sentences.zh: 邠繕甲兵，實帑廩，俾國用不闕，邊鄙粗寧，亦其功也。

translations.literal: Bin repaired armor and weapons and filled the granaries, so that state expenditures were not lacking and the frontier was roughly at peace—this too was his merit.
translations.idiomatic: He armed the troops, filled the storehouses, kept the treasury solvent, and brought a rough peace to the borders—those were his merits as well.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （《宣和書譜》云：邠末年留意縉紳，延客門下，知經史有用，乃課吏傳寫。）〉

translations.literal: (The Catalogue of Xuanhe Calligraphy says: in his later years Bin turned his attention to gentry, kept guests at his gate, knew that the classics and histories were useful, and had clerks copy them.) Closing editorial bracket.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Xuanhe Catalogue of Calligraphy says that in his last years Bin cultivated scholars, kept a salon, and set clerks to copying the classics once he saw their value.) Editorial bracket closing the comment block.

sentences.zh: 王章，大名南樂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhang was a native of Nanle in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang came from Nanle in Daming prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少為吏，給事使府。

translations.literal: In youth he was a clerk serving in a commissioner's office.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he clerked in a military commissioner's office.

sentences.zh: 同光初，隸樞密院，後歸本郡，累職至都孔目官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was attached to the Military Affairs Bureau; later he returned to his home prefecture and rose through posts to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang he served the Military Affairs Bureau, then returned home and rose to chief clerk of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後唐清泰末，屯駐捧聖都虞候張令昭作亂，逐節度使劉延皓，自稱留後，章以本職為令昭役使。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai in Later Tang, Zhang Lingzhao, garrison commander of the Honored Sacred Guard, rebelled, drove out military governor Liu Yanhao, styled himself acting governor, and Zhang in his original post served Lingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Later Tang's Qingtai era, garrison commander Zhang Lingzhao rebelled, expelled Liu Yanhao, and declared himself acting governor; Zhang served him in his old clerk's post.

sentences.zh: 末帝遣範延光討平之，搜索叛黨甚急。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor sent Fan Yanguang to suppress him; the search for rebels was very urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor sent Fan Yanguang to crush the revolt and hunted rebels relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 章之妻即白文珂之女也，文珂與副招討李敬周善，以章為托。

translations.literal: Zhang's wife was the daughter of Bai Wenke; Wenke was on good terms with deputy pacification commissioner Li Jingzhou and entrusted Zhang to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's wife was Bai Wenke's daughter; Wenke, who was close to Li Jingzhou, deputy pacification commissioner, asked Jingzhou to protect Zhang.

sentences.zh: 及攻下逆城，敬周匿之，載於橐駝褚中，竄至洛下，匿於敬周之私第。

translations.literal: When the rebel city was taken, Jingzhou hid him, loaded him in a camel saddlebag, fled to Luoyang, and concealed him in Jingzhou's private residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Jingzhou hid him in a camel pack, smuggled him to Luoyang, and sheltered him in his private house.

sentences.zh: 及末帝敗，章為省職，歷沔陽糧料使。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor was defeated, Zhang held a provincial post and served as grain commissioner of Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Last Emperor's fall Zhang held a provincial post and became grain commissioner of Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖典侍衛親軍，詔為都孔目官，從至河東，專委錢谷。

translations.literal: When Gaozu commanded the palace guard, he was ordered to be chief clerk, followed him to Hedong, and was entrusted solely with funds and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took charge of the palace guard he made Zhang chief clerk, brought him to Hedong, and put him in sole charge of finances.

sentences.zh: 國初，授三司使、檢校太傅，從征杜重威於鄴下。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he was made director of the Three Agencies and Honorary Grand Tutor, and followed the campaign against Du Chongwei at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding he became director of the Three Agencies and Honorary Grand Tutor and campaigned against Du Chongwei at Ye.

sentences.zh: 明年，高祖崩，隱帝即位，加檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: The next year Gaozu died and Emperor Yin succeeded; Zhang was made Honorary Grand Commandant and co-equal Grand Counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Gaozu died; Emperor Yin made him Honorary Grand Commandant and co-equal Grand Counsellor.

sentences.zh: 居無何，蒲、雍、岐三鎮畔。

translations.literal: Before long the three circuits of Pu, Yong, and Qi rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Pu, Yong, and Qi rebelled.

sentences.zh: 是時，契丹犯闕之後，國家新造，物力未充。

translations.literal: At this time, after the Khitan had violated the capital, the state was newly founded and material resources were not yet sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had just sacked the capital; the new dynasty's stores were still thin.

sentences.zh: 章與周太祖、史宏肇、楊邠等盡心王室，知無不為，罷不急之務，惜無用之費，收聚財賦，專事西征，軍旅所資，供饋無乏。

translations.literal: Zhang with Zhou Taizu, Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, and others devoted themselves to the royal house and did all they knew; they ended non-urgent tasks, spared useless expense, gathered taxes and levies, and focused on the western campaign, so that army supplies never lacked.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Zhou Taizu, Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, and the rest threw themselves into the throne's service, cut waste, gathered revenue, and fed the western campaign without fail.

sentences.zh: 及三叛平，賜與之外，國有餘積。

translations.literal: When the three rebellions were pacified, beyond rewards and gifts the state had surplus accumulations.
translations.idiomatic: After the three rebellions were crushed the treasury held a surplus beyond rewards and gifts.

sentences.zh: 然以專於權利，剝下過當，斂怨歸上，物論非之。

translations.literal: Yet because he was devoted to profit and power, he stripped the people beyond measure, gathered resentment onto the throne, and public opinion condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he clung to profit, squeezed the people too hard, and turned public resentment on the throne.

sentences.zh: 舊制，秋夏苗租，民稅一斛，別輸二升，謂之「雀鼠耗」。

translations.literal: By old regulation, for autumn and summer field rents the people paid one hu in tax and separately paid two sheng, called "sparrow-and-rat wastage."
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, for the summer and autumn grain tax each hu paid carried an extra two sheng called "sparrow-and-rat loss."

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，輸一斛者，別令輸二斗，目之為「省耗」。

translations.literal: In Qianyou, for each hu paid they were separately required to pay two dou, termed "provincial wastage."
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianyou, each hu delivered required an extra two dou called "provincial wastage."

sentences.zh: 百姓苦之。

translations.literal: The common people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: The people groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 又，官庫出納緡錢，皆以八十為陌，至是民輸者如舊，官給者以七十七為陌，遂為常式。

translations.literal: Again, in the government treasury's receipt and disbursement of cash strings, eighty counted as one hundred; from this time the people paid as before but the government paid at seventy-seven per hundred, and this became the regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: Government cash had long counted eighty coins as one string; now the people still paid at eighty while official payouts used seventy-seven, and that became permanent.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （《歸田錄》：用錢之法，自五代以來，以七十七為百，謂之「省陌」。

translations.literal: (The Record of Returning to the Fields says: the method of using money, since the Five Dynasties, has counted seventy-seven as one hundred, called "provincial short-count."
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang Xiu's Record of Returning to the Fields notes that since the Five Dynasties seventy-seven cash have counted as one hundred, called the "provincial short string."

sentences.zh: 今市井交易，又克其五，謂之「依除」。）〉

translations.literal: Today in market transactions they again deduct five, called "deduction by rule.") Closing editorial bracket.)
translations.idiomatic: In the markets today five more are shaved off, called "rule-based deduction.") Editorial bracket closing the comment block.

sentences.zh: 民有訴田者，雖無十數戶，章必命全州覆視，幸其廣有苗額，以增邦賦，曾未數年，民力大困。

translations.literal: When commoners sued over fields, even if there were not a dozen households, Zhang always ordered the whole prefecture to reinspect, hoping to broaden the assessed acreage and increase state levies; within only a few years the people's strength was greatly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever peasants disputed fields, even for a dozen households, Zhang ordered a full prefectural resurvey hoping to swell the tax rolls; within a few years the countryside was drained.

sentences.zh: 章與楊邠不喜儒士，郡官所請月俸，皆取不堪資軍者給之，謂之「閑雜物」，命所司高估其價，估定更添，謂之「擡估」，章亦不滿其意，隨事更令更添估。

translations.literal: Zhang and Yang Bin disliked Confucian scholars; for monthly salaries requested by prefectural officials they gave only goods unfit to supply the army, called "miscellaneous idle goods," ordered the responsible offices to overvalue them, and after valuation added more, called "inflated valuation"; Zhang was still not satisfied and ordered further inflation case by case.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Yang Bin disliked scholars; for officials' monthly pay they issued useless goods called "miscellaneous junk," had them overpriced, then marked them up again—"inflated valuation"—and Zhang often ordered yet another markup.

sentences.zh: 章急於財賦，峻於刑法，民有犯鹽礬酒曲之令，雖絲毫滴瀝，盡處極刑。

translations.literal: Zhang was urgent about revenue and severe in penal law; if the people violated orders on salt, alum, wine, or yeast, even a thread or a drop brought the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was frantic for revenue and harsh in law: the slightest breach of salt, alum, wine, or yeast monopolies brought death.

sentences.zh: 吏緣為奸，民不堪命。

translations.literal: Clerks took advantage to practice villainy, and the people could not bear their lot.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks preyed on them until life was unbearable.

sentences.zh: 章與楊邠同郡，尤為親愛，其獎用進拔者，莫非鄉舊。

translations.literal: Zhang and Yang Bin were from the same prefecture and were especially close; those they rewarded and promoted were none but hometown associates.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Yang Bin were fellow townsmen and intimate; everyone they promoted was a home-county man.

sentences.zh: 常輕視文臣，曰：「此等若與一把算子，未知顛倒，何益於事！

translations.literal: He often looked down on civil officials and said: "If you gave these men an abacus, they would not know which end is up—what good are they for affairs!
translations.idiomatic: He despised civil officials: "Give them an abacus and they could not tell head from tail—what use are they?

sentences.zh: 」後因私第開宴席，召賓客，史宏肇、蘇逢吉乘醉喧詬而罷。

translations.literal: " Later, because he opened a feast at his private residence and summoned guests, Shi Hongzhao and Su Fengji, drunk, shouted abuse and the gathering broke up.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he gave a feast at home; Shi Hongzhao and Su Fengji, drunk, quarreled loudly and the party broke up.

sentences.zh: 章自是忽忽不樂，潛求外任。

translations.literal: From this time Zhang was listless and unhappy and secretly sought an outer appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After that Zhang grew depressed and quietly sought a post outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 邠與宏肇深沮其意。

translations.literal: Bin and Hongzhao deeply obstructed his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Bin and Hongzhao blocked him firmly.

sentences.zh: 而私第數有怪異，章愈懷憂恐。

translations.literal: Yet his private residence repeatedly showed strange signs, and Zhang grew still more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Strange omens appeared at his house, and his fear deepened.

sentences.zh: 乾祐三年冬，與史宏肇、楊邠等遇害，夷其族。

translations.literal: In winter of the third year of Qianyou he was killed together with Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, and the others, and his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Qianyou 3 he was killed with Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, and the rest, and his clan was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 妻白氏，禍前數月而卒。

translations.literal: His wife, the Bai clan, had died several months before the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Bai had died months before the slaughter.

sentences.zh: 無子，惟一女，適戶部員外郎張貽肅，羸疾逾年，扶病就戮。

translations.literal: He had no sons, only a daughter married to Zhang Yisu, an outer official of the Ministry of Revenue; ill and wasted for more than a year, she was supported to her execution.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons, only a daughter married to Zhang Yisu of the Revenue Ministry; sick for more than a year, she was led to execution while barely able to stand.

sentences.zh: 閻晉卿者，忻州人也。

translations.literal: Yan Jinqing was a native of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jinqing came from Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 家世富豪，少仕並門，歷職至客將，高祖在鎮，頗見信用。

translations.literal: His family had been wealthy for generations; in youth he served at Bing Gate and rose through posts to guest general; when Gaozu was in his commandery he was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: His family was rich; he entered service at Taiyuan and rose to guest general, winning Gaozu's trust when Gaozu governed there.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，歷閣門使，判四方館。

translations.literal: In Qianyou he served successively as gate commissioner and concurrently judged the Four Directions Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianyou he became gate commissioner and overseer of the hostel for foreign envoys.

sentences.zh: 未幾，關西亂，郭從義討趙思綰於京兆，晉卿偏師以攻賊壘。

translations.literal: Before long the Guanxi region was in turmoil; Guo Congyi campaigned against Zhao Sixuan at Jingzhao, and Jinqing led a detached force to attack the rebel stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the west rebelled; as Guo Congyi besieged Zhao Sixuan at Chang'an, Jinqing led a flank force against the rebel camps.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·李韜傳》：周祖征三叛，韜從白文珂攻河中，兵傅其城。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Li Tao in the Song History: when Zhou Taizu campaigned against the three rebellions, Tao followed Bai Wenke in attacking Hezhong and pressed the army against the city.
translations.idiomatic: (The Song History biography of Li Tao records that when Zhou Taizu marched against the three rebels, Tao followed Bai Wenke against Hezhong and invested the city.

sentences.zh: 文珂夜詣周祖議犒軍，留韜城下。

translations.literal: Wenke by night went to Zhou Taizu to discuss rewarding the army and left Tao below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wenke went by night to Zhou Taizu to arrange rewards for the army and left Tao below the walls.

sentences.zh: 時營柵未備，李守貞乘虛來襲，營中忽見火發，知賊驟至，惶怖失據。

translations.literal: At the time the camp palisade was not yet complete; Li Shouzhen seized the opening to attack; fire suddenly broke out in the camp, they knew the enemy had come in a rush, and in terror lost their footing.
translations.idiomatic: The camp was unfinished when Li Shouzhen struck; flames leapt up, the men knew the enemy was upon them, and panic spread.

sentences.zh: 客省使閻晉卿率左右數十人，遇韜於月城側，謂韜曰：「事急矣。

translations.literal: Guest Bureau commissioner Yan Jinqing led several tens of his attendants, met Tao beside the moon wall, and said to Tao: "The matter is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jinqing of the Guest Bureau met Tao by the moon wall with a few dozen men and said, "This is desperate.

sentences.zh: 城中人悉被黃紙甲，為火光所照，色俱白，此殊易辨，奈軍士無鬥志何！

translations.literal: All in the city wear yellow-paper armor; lit by the fire they all show white—this is very easy to tell apart, but what can be done when the soldiers have no fighting spirit!
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the city wears armor of yellow paper; in the firelight it all looks white and is easy to spot—but our men have no heart to fight!

sentences.zh: 」韜憤怒曰：「豈有食君祿而不為國致死耶！

translations.literal: " Tao said in anger: "How can one eat the ruler's salary and not die for the state!
translations.idiomatic: " Tao cried angrily, "Who eats the ruler's grain and will not die for the state?

sentences.zh: 」即援槊而進，軍中死士十餘輩，隨韜犯賊鋒。

translations.literal: " He at once took his spear and advanced; more than ten determined men in the army followed Tao against the enemy front.
translations.idiomatic: " He seized his spear and charged; a dozen die-hards followed him into the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 蒲有猛將，躍馬持戈擬韜，韜刺之，洞胸而墜，又連殺數十人，蒲軍遂潰，因擊大破之。）〉

translations.literal: Hezhong had a fierce general who leaped on his horse and aimed his halberd at Tao; Tao stabbed him, pierced his chest, and he fell; he then killed several tens more in succession, the Hezhong army broke, and they struck a great defeat. Closing editorial bracket.)
translations.idiomatic: A Hezhong champion charged Tao with a halberd; Tao ran him through the chest and cut down dozens more until the Hezhong army broke and fled.) Editorial bracket closing the comment block.

sentences.zh: 賊平，為內客省使，丁父憂，起復前職。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was made commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau; on his father's mourning he was recalled to his former post before the mourning term ended.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion he became Inner Guests commissioner; when his father died he was recalled from mourning to the same post.

sentences.zh: 時宣徽使闕，晉卿以職次事望，合當其任，既而久稽拜命，晉卿頗怨執政。

translations.literal: At the time the post of palace attendant commissioner was vacant; by seniority and public expectation Jinqing ought to have had it, but the appointment was long delayed, and Jinqing resented those in power.
translations.idiomatic: The palace attendant commissionership was vacant; by seniority Jinqing should have had it, but the appointment dragged on and he grew bitter toward the ministers.

sentences.zh: 會李業等謀殺楊、史，詔晉卿謀之。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Ye and others plotted to kill Yang and Shi; the emperor ordered Jinqing to plot with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ye plotted to kill Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao, the emperor enlisted Jinqing in the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 晉卿退詣宏肇，將告其事，宏肇不見。

translations.literal: Jinqing withdrew and went to Hongzhao intending to inform him, but Hongzhao would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing then went to warn Hongzhao, who refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 晉卿憂事不果，夜懸高祖御容於中堂，泣禱於前，遲明戎服入朝。

translations.literal: Jinqing feared the affair would not succeed; at night he hung Gaozu's imperial portrait in the central hall, wept and prayed before it, and at dawn entered court in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing failure, he hung Gaozu's portrait in his hall, wept before it through the night, and went to court at dawn in armor.

sentences.zh: 內難既作，以晉卿權侍衛馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When the inner turmoil broke out, Jinqing was made acting commander of the palace guard cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace coup began he was made acting commander of the palace guard cavalry.

sentences.zh: 北郊兵敗，晉卿乃自殺於家。

translations.literal: When the army was defeated at the northern suburb, Jinqing then killed himself at home.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at the northern suburb he killed himself at home.

sentences.zh: 聶文進，并州人。

translations.literal: Nie Wenjin was a native of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Wenjin came from Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少給事於高祖帳下，高祖鎮太原，甚見委用，職至兵馬押司官。

translations.literal: In youth he served in Gaozu's personal staff; when Gaozu held Taiyuan he was greatly entrusted and rose to the post of horse-and-army custody officer.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served in Gaozu's household; when Gaozu governed Taiyuan he rose to horse-and-army custody officer.

sentences.zh: 高祖入汴，授樞密院承旨，歷領軍、屯衛大將軍，遷右衛大將軍，仍領舊職。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Bian he was made bearer of the Military Affairs Bureau, served successively as general of the garrison guards, and was transferred to great general of the Right Guard while still holding his old post.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took Bian he became bearer of the Military Affairs Bureau, rose through garrison commands to great general of the Right Guard, and kept his old duties.

sentences.zh: 遇周太祖出征，稍至驕橫，久未遷改，深所怨望，與李業輩構成變亂。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu went on campaign he grew somewhat arrogant; long without promotion he harbored deep resentment and with Li Ye and his faction engineered the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu marched out he grew arrogant; passed over for promotion too long, he joined Li Ye in plotting revolt.

sentences.zh: 史宏肇等遇害之前夕，文進與同黨預作宣詔，制置朝廷之事，凡關文字，並出文進之手。

translations.literal: On the eve of Shi Hongzhao and the others being killed, Wenjin with his faction prepared proclamations in advance, arranged court affairs, and all documents issued from Wenjin's hand.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the ministers' deaths Wenjin and his allies drafted the edicts in advance and controlled every document of state.

sentences.zh: 明日難作，文進點閱兵籍，征發軍眾，指揮取舍，以為己任，內外咨稟，前後填咽。

translations.literal: The next day when the turmoil broke out, Wenjin inspected military registers, mobilized troops, and directed who was taken or spared as his own duty; reports inward and outward jammed the gates.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup came the next day he mustered troops from the registers, decided who marched and who stayed, and the court was choked with his orders.

sentences.zh: 太祖在鄴被構，初謂文進不預其事，驗其事跡，方知文進亂階之首也，大詬詈之。

translations.literal: Taizu at Ye was framed; at first he thought Wenjin was not involved, but when the traces were verified he knew Wenjin was chief of the steps to chaos and cursed him bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: At Ye, Zhou Taizu first thought Wenjin innocent; when the evidence came in he saw Wenjin had led the plot and cursed him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 太祖過封丘，帝次於北郊，文進告太后曰：「臣在此，請宮中勿憂。

translations.literal: When Taizu passed Fengqiu the emperor halted at the northern suburb; Wenjin told the empress dowager: "Your servant is here—please do not worry within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: As Taizu passed Fengqiu the emperor camped at the northern suburb; Wenjin told the empress dowager, "I am here—the palace need not fear.

sentences.zh: 」兵散之後，文進召同黨痛飲，歌笑自若。

translations.literal: " After the army scattered, Wenjin summoned his faction for heavy drinking and sang and laughed as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " After the army broke he drank heavily with his allies, singing as if nothing were wrong.

sentences.zh: 遲明，帝遇禍，文進奔竄，為軍士所追，梟其首。

translations.literal: Near dawn the emperor met calamity; Wenjin fled in panic, was pursued by soldiers, and his head was displayed.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the emperor was killed; Wenjin fled, was caught by soldiers, and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 後贊，為飛龍使。

translations.literal: Hou Zan served as commissioner of the Flying Dragon Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zan was commissioner of the Flying Dragon Guard.

sentences.zh: 贊母本倡家也，與父同郡，往來其家，生贊。

translations.literal: Zan's mother had originally been of a singing-house family; she and his father were from the same prefecture; he visited her household and she bore Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's mother had been a entertainer; his father, a fellow townsman, visited her house and Zan was born.

sentences.zh: 從職四方，父未嘗離郡，贊既長，疑其所生。

translations.literal: He followed office to the four directions while his father never left the prefecture; when Zan grew up he doubted who had fathered him.
translations.idiomatic: Zan served far and wide while his father never left the county; grown up, he doubted his birth.

sentences.zh: 及為內職，不欲父之來，寓書以致其意。

translations.literal: When he held an inner post he did not want his father to come and sent a letter to convey his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held a palace post he wrote telling his father not to come.

sentences.zh: 父自郡至京師，直抵其第，贊不得已而奉之。

translations.literal: His father came from the prefecture to the capital, went straight to his residence, and Zan had no choice but to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: His father came to the capital anyway and walked into his house; Zan had to receive him.

sentences.zh: 乾祐末，宰相楊祐、侍衛親軍使史宏肇執權，贊以久次未遷，頗懷怨望，乃與樞密承旨聶文進等構變。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianyou chief minister Yang Bin and palace guard commander Shi Hongzhao held power; Zan, long passed over for promotion, harbored resentment and with Military Affairs bearer Nie Wenjin and others engineered the coup.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qianyou, with Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao in power, Zan—passed over too long—joined Nie Wenjin in plotting the coup.

sentences.zh: 及難作，贊與同黨更侍帝側，剖判戎事，且防間言。

translations.literal: When the turmoil broke out, Zan with his faction attended the emperor in turn, decided military affairs, and also guarded against slander.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup began Zan and his allies kept watch beside the emperor, ran military affairs, and blocked rumor.

sentences.zh: 北郊兵敗，贊竄歸兗州，慕容彥超執之以獻，有司鞫贊伏罪，周太祖命誅之。

translations.literal: When the army was defeated at the northern suburb, Zan fled to Yanzhou; Murong Yanchao seized him and presented him; the judicial offices interrogated him until he confessed guilt, and Zhou Taizu ordered his execution.
translations.idiomatic: After the northern-suburb defeat he fled to Yanzhou; Murong Yanchao seized him and handed him over; tried and convicted, he was executed on Zhou Taizu's order.

sentences.zh: 郭允明者，小名竇十，河東人也。

translations.literal: Guo Yunming, whose childhood name was Dou Ten, was a native of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yunming, nicknamed Dou Ten, came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 幼隸河東制置使範徽柔，被誅，允明遂為高祖廝養，服勤既久，頗得高祖之歡心。

translations.literal: In youth he was attached to Hedong commissioner Fan Huirou; when Huirou was executed, Yunming became Gaozu's menial servant; after long diligent service he won Gaozu's favor.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he served Fan Huirou, Hedong commissioner; when Fan was executed he became Gaozu's servant and, after years of loyal service, won his favor.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮太原，稍歷牙職，及即位，累遷至翰林茶酒使兼鞍轡庫使。

translations.literal: When Gaozu held Taiyuan he gradually passed through aide posts; when he took the throne Yunming was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin tea-and-wine commissioner and concurrently saddlery-store commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu governed Taiyuan he rose through the staff; at accession he became Hanlin tea-and-wine commissioner and keeper of the saddlery store.

sentences.zh: 隱帝嗣位，尤見親狎，每恃寵驕縱，略無禮敬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yin succeeded he was especially intimate with Yunming, who relied on favor to act arrogantly and showed scarcely any respect.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yin he was a favorite and, trusting in that favor, behaved with arrogant disrespect.

sentences.zh: 與相州節度使郭謹以同宗之故，頗交結。

translations.literal: With Guo Jin, military governor of Xiangzhou, he was on rather close terms because they shared the same clan name.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Guo Jin, military governor of Xiangzhou, because they shared a clan name.

sentences.zh: 謹在鎮，允明常賫禦酒以遺之，不以僭上犯禁為意。

translations.literal: While Jin was in his commandery, Yunming often sent imperial wine as gifts to him without minding that this usurped the throne's prerogative and violated prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: While Jin governed his circuit Yunming often sent him imperial wine without caring that it was a forbidden gift of the throne's property.

sentences.zh: 其他輕率，悉皆類此，執政大臣頗姑息之。

translations.literal: His other rash acts were all of this kind, and the ministers in power largely indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: His other follies were of the same sort, and the chief ministers mostly looked the other way.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉使荊南，車服導從，有同節度使將，州縣郵驛，奔馳畏懾，節度使高保融承迎不暇。

translations.literal: Once on a mission to Jingnan his carriage, insignia, and escort were like those of a military governor on campaign; prefectures, counties, and relay stations raced in fear; military governor Gao Baorong could scarcely keep up with receiving him.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Jingnan he traveled with the pomp of a military governor; every post station scrambled in fear, and Gao Baorong could barely keep pace with his welcomes.

sentences.zh: 允明潛使人步度城壁之高庳、池隍之廣隘，以動荊人，冀得重賄。

translations.literal: Yunming secretly sent men to pace-measure the height and low points of the walls and the breadth and narrowness of the moats to impress the people of Jing, hoping for heavy bribes.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly had men measure the walls and moats to intimidate the Jingnan people and extract heavy bribes.

sentences.zh: 乾祐末，兼飛龍使。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianyou he was made concurrent commissioner of the Flying Dragon Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qianyou he was also made commissioner of the Flying Dragon Guard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，與李業輩構變，楊邠等諸子，允明親刃之於朝堂西廡下。

translations.literal: Before long he joined Li Ye and his faction in engineering the coup; Yang Bin and the other ministers Yunming personally cut down with his blade beneath the western veranda of the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined Li Ye in the coup; Yunming himself slew Yang Bin and the other ministers with a blade under the western veranda of the hall.

sentences.zh: 王章女婿戶部員外郎張貽肅，血流逆註，聞者哀之。

translations.literal: Wang Zhang's son-in-law Zhang Yisu, outer official of the Ministry of Revenue, had blood flowing back upward; those who heard of it pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang's son-in-law Zhang Yisu of the Revenue Ministry bled until the blood seemed to flow backward; all who saw it were moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 及北郊之敗，允明迫帝就民舍，手行弒逆，尋亦自殺。

translations.literal: When the army was defeated at the northern suburb, Yunming forced the emperor into a commoner's house and with his own hands committed regicide; soon after he killed himself as well.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at the northern suburb Yunming drove the emperor into a private house and murdered him with his own hands, then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 劉銖，陜州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhu was a native of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhu came from Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 少事梁邵王朱友誨為牙將。

translations.literal: In youth he served Prince Shao of Liang, Zhu Youhui, as an aide-de-camp.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served Liang's Prince Shao, Zhu Youhui, as an aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，高祖為侍衛親軍都指揮使，與銖有舊，乃表為內職。

translations.literal: In Tianfu of Jin, when Gaozu was commander of the palace guard, he and Zhu were old acquaintances, and he memorialized to make Zhu an inner-office official.
translations.idiomatic: During Jin's Tianfu era, when Gaozu commanded the palace guard, he knew Zhu of old and had him appointed to the inner service.

sentences.zh: 高祖出鎮並門，用為左都押牙。

translations.literal: When Gaozu went out to govern Bing Gate he employed Zhu as left chief aide-de-camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu went to govern Taiyuan he made Zhu his left chief aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 銖性慘毒好殺，高祖以為勇斷類己，深委遇之。

translations.literal: Zhu's nature was cruel, poisonous, and fond of killing; Gaozu thought him brave and decisive like himself and deeply entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was cruel and bloodthirsty; Gaozu saw his own ruthless decisiveness in him and relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 國初，授永興軍節度使，從定汴、洛、移鎮青州，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he was made military governor of the Yongxing army; he followed in pacifying Bian and Luo, was transferred to govern Qingzhou, and was made co-equal Grand Counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding he became military governor of Yongxing, helped pacify Bian and Luoyang, was moved to Qingzhou, and was made co-equal Grand Counsellor.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，加檢校太師、兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yin succeeded he was further made Honorary Grand Preceptor and concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yin came to the throne he was given the honorary rank of Grand Preceptor and made Palace Attendant as well.

sentences.zh: 銖立法深峻，令行禁止，吏民有過，不問輕重，未嘗貸免。

translations.literal: Zhu's laws were deep and severe; orders were enforced and prohibitions observed; when officials or commoners offended, without asking lightness or heaviness he never granted pardon.
translations.idiomatic: His laws were harsh and absolute: any offense, great or small, was never forgiven.

sentences.zh: 每親事，小有忤旨，即令倒曳而出，至數百步外方止，膚體無完者。

translations.literal: Whenever he personally handled affairs, if there was the slightest offense against his intent he had the man dragged out head downward and not stopped until several hundred paces away; not an inch of skin was left whole.
translations.idiomatic: At court the slightest slip brought an order to drag the offender headfirst for hundreds of paces; few survived the ordeal with whole skin.

sentences.zh: 每杖人，遣雙杖對下，謂之「合歡杖」；

translations.literal: Whenever he beat someone he had two clubs strike together, called the "joyous-clubs beating";
translations.idiomatic: When he flogged a man he used two clubs at once, called the "paired-club beating";

sentences.zh: 或杖人如其歲數，謂之「隨年杖」。

translations.literal: or he beat a man according to his age in years, called the "age-matched beating."
translations.idiomatic: or he gave as many strokes as the victim's age, called the "year-for-year beating."

sentences.zh: 在任擅行賦斂，每秋苗一畝率錢三千，夏苗一畝錢二千，以備公用，部內畏之，脅肩重跡。

translations.literal: In office he levied taxes on his own authority; for each mu of autumn crop he charged three thousand cash, for summer crop two thousand per mu, to supply public use; within his circuit they feared him and walked hunched shoulder to shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: He taxed at will—three thousand cash per mu of autumn grain, two thousand for summer—and his subjects shrank from him in the roads.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，淄、青大蝗，銖下令捕蝗，略無遺漏，田苗無害。

translations.literal: In Qianyou there was a great locust plague in Zi and Qing; Zhu ordered locusts captured without omission, and the fields were unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou, when locusts ravaged Zi and Qing, he ordered a thorough hunt that left the crops untouched.

sentences.zh: 先是，濱海郡邑，皆有兩浙回易務，厚取民利，自置刑禁，追攝王民，前後長吏利其厚賂，不能禁止。

translations.literal: Earlier, in coastal prefectures and districts there were Two-Zhe exchange offices that took heavy profit from the people, set up their own punishments, and pursued and seized the ruler's subjects; successive chief officials profited from their heavy bribes and could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal towns had long hosted Two-Zhe trade offices that extorted the people, enforced their own punishments, and seized subjects of the throne; local governors took their bribes and dared not stop them.

sentences.zh: 銖即告所部，不得與吳越征負，擅行追攝，浙人惕息，莫敢幹命。

translations.literal: Zhu at once informed his circuit that they must not collect debts for Wu-Yue or pursue and seize on their own; the people of Zhe drew in their breath and none dared interfere with his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu forbade his region to collect debts for Wu-Yue or seize people on their behalf; the Zhe merchants fell silent and none dared defy him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷懼銖之剛戾難制，因前浙州刺史郭瓊自海州用兵還，過青州，遂留之，即以府彥卿代銖，銖即時受代。

translations.literal: The court feared Zhu's harsh obstinacy was hard to control; because the former prefect of Zhe Guo Qiong was returning from campaigning at Haizhou and passed Qingzhou, he was kept there and Murong Yanchao was put in Zhu's place; Zhu at once accepted transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Zhu's brutal temper, the court kept Guo Qiong—returning from Haizhou through Qingzhou—and sent Murong Yanchao to replace him; Zhu yielded immediately.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （《隆平集》《郭瓊傳》云：劉銖守平盧，稱疾不朝，隱帝疑其叛，詔瓊領兵屯青州。

translations.literal: (The Longping Collection and Biography of Guo Qiong say: Liu Zhu guarded Pinglu, claimed illness and did not attend court; Emperor Yin suspected rebellion and ordered Qiong to lead troops to garrison Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: (The Longping Collection biography of Guo Qiong records that Liu Zhu, holding Pinglu, pleaded illness and stayed away; the emperor suspected revolt and sent Qiong to camp at Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 銖將害之，張宴伏兵幕下，瓊無懼色，銖亦不敢發。

translations.literal: Zhu intended to harm him and spread a feast with armed men hidden beneath the canopy; Qiong showed no fear, and Zhu also did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu planned to kill him and set armed men under the feast canopy; Qiong showed no fear, and Zhu did not dare strike.

sentences.zh: 瓊為言去就禍福，銖趨召。）〉

translations.literal: Qiong spoke of the fortune and misfortune of staying or leaving, and Zhu hurried to answer the summons. Closing editorial bracket.)
translations.idiomatic: Qiong explained the consequences of staying or going, and Zhu hurried to court.) Editorial bracket closing the comment block.

sentences.zh: 離鎮之日，有私鹽數屋，雜以糞穢，填塞諸井，以土平之。

translations.literal: On the day he left his commandery there were several rooms of private salt mixed with filth; he stuffed the wells and leveled them with earth.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving his post he left several rooms of illicit salt mixed with filth, stuffed the wells, and buried them under earth.

sentences.zh: 彥卿發其事以聞，銖奉朝請久之，每潛戟手於史宏肇、楊邠第。

translations.literal: Yanchao exposed the matter and reported it; Zhu attended court for a long time as a court gentleman, and often secretly clenched his fists outside the residences of Shi Hongzhao and Yang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao reported the salt; Zhu lingered at court as a gentleman-in-attendance and often passed Hongzhao's and Bin's mansions with clenched fists.

sentences.zh: 會李業輩同誅宏肇等，銖喜，謂業輩曰：「君等可謂僂羅兒矣。

translations.literal: When Li Ye and his faction jointly executed Hongzhao and the others, Zhu rejoiced and said to Ye's group: "You gentlemen may be called lackey-boys indeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ye's faction killed Hongzhao and the rest, Zhu rejoiced and told them, "You fellows have done the master's dirty work at last.

sentences.zh: 」尋以銖權知開封府事，周太祖親族及王峻家，並為銖所害。

translations.literal: " Soon Zhu was made acting administrator of the Kaifeng prefecture; Zhou Taizu's kin and Wang Jun's household were all harmed by Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then made acting prefect of Kaifeng and slaughtered Zhou Taizu's relatives and Wang Jun's household.

sentences.zh: 周太祖入京城，執之下獄。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu entered the capital he was seized and put in prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu entered the capital he was arrested.

sentences.zh: 銖謂妻曰：「我則死矣，君應與人為婢耳！

translations.literal: Zhu said to his wife: "I shall die; you will have to become someone's maidservant!
translations.idiomatic: Zhu told his wife, "I am as good as dead—you will end someone's servant girl!

sentences.zh: 」妻曰：「明公所為如是，雅合為之。

translations.literal: " His wife said: "What my lord has done is just such as this—entirely fitting that it should be so.
translations.idiomatic: " His wife replied, "Given what you have done, that is only fitting."

sentences.zh: 」周太祖遣人讓銖曰：「昔日與公常同事漢室，寧無故人之情，家屬屠滅，公雖奉君命，加之酷毒，一何忍哉！

translations.literal: " Zhou Taizu sent someone to rebuke Zhu: "In former days I often served the Han house together with you—was there not the feeling of old friends? Your slaughter of families—though you followed the ruler's command, to add such cruelty—how could you be so pitiless!
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu sent a messenger to reproach him: "We once served the Han together—had you no memory of friendship? You butchered whole families on the emperor's order, yet added cruelty of your own—how pitiless!

sentences.zh: 公家亦有妻子，還顧念否？

translations.literal: Your own household also has wife and children—do you not look back and consider them?
translations.idiomatic: You too have a wife and children—do you never think of them?

sentences.zh: 」銖但稱死罪。

translations.literal: " Zhu could only plead guilty unto death.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu could only plead for death.

sentences.zh: 遂啟太后，並一子誅之，而釋其妻。

translations.literal: He then informed the empress dowager, executed Zhu together with one son, and released his wife.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the empress dowager, executed Zhu and one son, and spared his wife.

sentences.zh: 周太祖踐阼，詔賜銖妻陜州莊宅各一區。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu took the throne he issued an edict bestowing on Zhu's wife one estate and one residence in Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu took the throne he granted Zhu's wife an estate and a house in Shaanzhou.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial bracket opening a comment block.

sentences.zh: （《五代史闕文》：漢隱帝朝，銖為開封尹，周祖自鄴起兵，銖盡誅周祖之家子孫婦女十數人，極其慘毒。

translations.literal: (Supplemental Texts to the History of the Five Dynasties: in the court of Han Emperor Yin, Zhu was prefect of Kaifeng; when Zhou Taizu raised troops from Ye, Zhu executed more than ten of Zhou Taizu's household—descendants and women—with extreme cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: (The Supplemental Texts to the History of the Five Dynasties says that under Emperor Yin, Zhu as Kaifeng prefect slaughtered more than a dozen of Zhou Taizu's kin—men, women, and children—with appalling cruelty when Taizu marched from Ye.

sentences.zh: 及隱帝遇害，周祖以漢太后令，收銖下獄，使人責之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yin met harm, Zhou Taizu on the Han empress dowager's order seized Zhu and put him in prison, and sent someone to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor was killed, Taizu, acting on the empress dowager's order, imprisoned Zhu and sent a messenger to condemn him.

sentences.zh: 銖對曰：「某為漢家戮叛族耳，不知其他。

translations.literal: Zhu replied: "I merely executed the rebel clan for the house of Han—I know nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu answered, "I only destroyed a rebel clan for the Han—I know nothing beyond that.

sentences.zh: 」周祖怒，遂殺之。）〉

translations.literal: " Zhou Taizu in anger then killed him. Closing editorial bracket.)
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu in fury had him killed.) Editorial bracket closing the comment block.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：臣觀漢之亡也，豈系於天命哉！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: This subject observes that the fall of Han—was it really bound to fate!
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: In my view, did the fall of Later Han truly hang on Heaven's mandate?

sentences.zh: 蓋委用不得其人，聽斷不符於理故也。

translations.literal: It was rather that the men entrusted were not the right ones, and judgments did not accord with reason.
translations.idiomatic: It came rather from putting power in the wrong hands and deciding affairs without reason.

sentences.zh: 且如宏肇之淫刑，楊邠之秕政，李業、晉卿之設計，文進、允明之狂且，雖使成王為君，周公作相，亦不能保宗社之安，延歲月之命，況隱帝、逢吉之徒，其能免乎！

translations.literal: Consider Hongzhao's excessive punishments, Yang Bin's chaff-like government, the plots of Li Ye and Jinqing, the madness and folly of Wenjin and Yunming—even if King Cheng were ruler and the Duke of Zhou chief minister, they could not have preserved the altars of state or prolonged the dynasty's months and years; how much less could Emperor Yin, Fengji, and men of that sort escape!
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao's savage punishments, Yang Bin's hollow governance, the intrigues of Li Ye and Jinqing, the reckless folly of Wenjin and Yunming—even with King Cheng on the throne and the Duke of Zhou as minister the altars could not have stood nor the dynasty endured; how then could Emperor Yin, Su Fengji, and their like have been spared?

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「大君有命，開國承家，小人勿用，必亂邦也。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "The great ruler has a command—to found states and inherit houses; do not employ petty men, for they will surely disorder the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "The great ruler enfeoffs states and establishes houses, but petty men must not be used—they will surely bring the realm to ruin."

sentences.zh: 」當乾祐之末也，何斯言之驗歟！

translations.literal: " At the end of Qianyou, how was this saying fulfilled!
translations.idiomatic: " At the close of Qianyou, how fully those words were proved!

sentences.zh: 惟劉銖之忍酷，又安能逭於一死乎！

translations.literal: As for Liu Zhu's cruel ruthlessness, how could he escape a single death!
translations.idiomatic: As for Liu Zhu's cruelty, how could he have escaped death?
